1	# T-028 design — a concept is its id; its names are forms; `canonical_en` is our label
2	
3	_Written 2026-11-12 by an Opus-class designer under the owner's instruction "Opus to write design files that must be written first", on the delegated resolution of OD-03. Plan document: it changes no script, schema, row or ruling. Every count is given as the command that produces it; re-run it. SQL marked **sketch** is a shape, not a file to paste unread. Canadian English._
4	
5	_Revised 2026-11-13, after the T-028 pilot (`scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/pilot/T-028-report.md`) and the fold of T-026: no pointer reaches `term_aliases` by `rowid` (SQLite cannot declare a foreign key on one and `emit_batch_sql.py` does not carry implicit rowids), so T-026's junction is keyed and T-028 remaps it by key to `form_id`; `attestation` keeps T-026's `DEFAULT`; the judge, reason and former label of every label set by judgment get one typed home, `term_label_picks`, which also holds the base route's rationale; the refusals of `rename-term` and `mint-term-from-catalogue` are kept, and one cross-language question is left to the owner; `label_is_instrument_term` is renamed `label_is_attested_form`. Where the 2026-11-12 text and this revision differ, the revision governs._
6	
7	## 0. Verdict
8	
9	**The one table that holds a form is `term_aliases`.** No new forms table is built. T-026 puts the attestation and locator columns on it (names fixed in section 4 so the two tasks agree). T-028 then rebuilds it to one row per **occurrence**, keyed by a new `form_id` (equal to each existing row's `rowid`), with a unique occurrence index in place of today's primary key `(term_id, alias, language)`, and adds `usage_type`. In the same migration it remaps T-026's search-to-form junction from the old key to `form_id`, by key, and adds `term_label_picks`, the one home of the judge, the reason and the former label of a label set by judgment (OD-38). A concept's identity stays `terms.term_id`; its equivalence class is its member rows in `term_aliases`. **`terms.canonical_en` stays `TEXT NOT NULL`, as our English descriptive label: never written as a form, never read first.** (A new label is screened against other concepts' labels and attested forms so that one phrase does not point at two concepts, section 8.) Whether the label is also an instrument's term, and the name shown (E1), are derived by one view, `v_term_names`; the only stored choice is the label itself, changed by `rename-term` with its warrant. Five writers change: the two name screens (`_name_holder`, `_near_terms`) become attestation-aware and stop making English the pivot for a non-English name; `add-term` gains a base route that mints a concept with its first attested form and stops forcing a non-English concept's label to sit inside the source's phrase (the defect AT-25 exposes); `rename-term` stops writing our former label as a form or as a `scope_note` trailer and gains `--from-form`, every route naming its judge; `add-alias` refuses the legacy relation values and records an occurrence, not a key.
10	
11	**Confidence.** Medium-high (about 75%) that `term_aliases` is the right single home: the alternative (`term_forms`, the 2026-11-06 matrix design) leaves 2382 baseline rows in a second table that can never be emptied (section 2). Medium (about 60%) on the display rule's tie-break (section 7, rule 2), which is deterministic but arbitrary when several English instruments use different forms.
12	
13	**Owner's call.** None is outstanding: OD-03 is resolved under delegation (`grep -F "OD-03 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1`; its check is `not required`), reversible by the owner. The points at which the owner may disagree are listed in section 15; the one most likely to matter is the tie-break of section 7.
14	
15	## 1. What the rulings require
16	
17	| Ruling (find it with) | Requirement | Met by |
18	|---|---|---|
19	| OD-03 (delegated), `grep -n -F 'OD-03: forms table' references/project-standards.md` | identity is the neutral id; names are rows of one forms table, one row per occurrence with language, jurisdiction, source; `canonical_en` our label, never a form; label basis derived; display by E1; a stored choice only where no derivation decides | sections 3, 6, 7 |
20	| Sixth statement 2026-11-06, `grep -n -F 'a concept is an equivalence class of forms' references/project-standards.md` | equivalence class; usage type and attestation per form; disfavoured forms kept; conflation recorded per occurrence, not resolved | member rows; `usage_type`; T-026's `attestation`; conflation derived (section 5) |
21	| Seventh statement 2026-11-06, `grep -n -F 'base grounds itself' references/project-standards.md` | a base form carries its own source columns (URL, page, line), not an `evidence_sources` row | T-026's locator columns; `add-term` base route (section 8) |
22	| Eighth statement 2026-11-06, `grep -n -F 'English labels are allowed on non-English-origin concepts' references/project-standards.md` | an English label allowed, marked as ours; the instrument's phrase kept as a form; no English form until an English-jurisdiction source uses one; no column read, matched or ranked first | `canonical_en` as label; `v_term_names.label_is_attested_form`; screens per language (section 8) |
23	| E1 and E4, `grep -n -E '^\| E1 |^\| E4 ' references/project-standards.md` | E1: named by the instrument's own phrase until an English-language instrument of a P1+P2+P3 jurisdiction names it. E4: model-generated and unrecorded aliases stay as flagged search aids, never vocabulary, never deleted | `v_term_names` rules (section 7); screens read attested forms only (section 8) |
24	| CLAUDE.md rule 5 and the 2026-11-06 schema-shape statement | one home per fact; one value per cell | one forms table; `usage_type` and `attestation` in their own cells; legacy `alias_type` values frozen (section 5) |
25	
26	## 2. Why `term_aliases`, not a new `term_forms`
27	
28	- **One home.** `term_aliases` already holds every name the base has (`select count(*) from term_aliases`). Its rows were inserted by the 057 baseline (`grep -c 'INSERT INTO "term_aliases"' scripts/migrations/057_baseline_2026-08-12.sql`), and the 2026-09-16 ruling retires data rows in place, never deleting them. A new `term_forms` beside it leaves those rows where they are forever: either copied (two homes) or reached through a union view (the matrix design's `v_base_lookup`), which is two homes joined at read time.
29	- **The matrix design's two objections are answered in place.** (i) "The PK has no jurisdiction or source": the rebuild replaces the PK by a surrogate key and an occurrence index that includes jurisdiction and locator (section 3). (ii) "It mixes model seeds with attested forms": T-026's typed `attestation` separates them in a cell, and every vocabulary read filters on it (section 8).
30	- **The name stays.** Renaming the table would make every caller a sweep item (`git grep -l -F term_aliases -- scripts schemas .github .claude skills ':(exclude)scripts/migrations'` and the prose `git grep` of the task file) for a legibility gain only; a row of `term_aliases` is documented as "a form of the concept, or a related search string" (section 5).
31	
32	## 3. The table after T-026 and T-028 (sketch)
33	
34	```sql
35	-- sketch: term_aliases after T-028's rebuild. Columns marked (T-026) are added by T-026 first.
36	CREATE TABLE term_aliases (
37	    form_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,   -- assigned once, in the migration, from the old rowid; nothing stored points by rowid
38	    term_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
39	    alias               TEXT NOT NULL,                       -- the form, verbatim
40	    language            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EN',
41	    alias_type          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (alias_type IN
42	                            ('SYNONYM','TRANSLATION','NARROWER','BROADER','DEPRECATED','DOMAIN')),  -- unchanged; section 5
43	    jurisdiction        TEXT,
44	    notes               TEXT,
45	    observation_id      INTEGER REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
46	    attestation         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unrecorded' CHECK (attestation IN
47	                            ('instrument','other_source','owner_supplied','model_seed','unrecorded')),  -- (T-026; the DEFAULT is kept)
48	    source_url          TEXT CHECK (source_url IS NULL OR source_url GLOB 'http*://*'),             -- (T-026)
49	    source_page         TEXT,                                                                       -- (T-026)
50	    source_line         INTEGER CHECK (source_line IS NULL OR source_line > 0),                    -- (T-026)
51	    source_clause       TEXT,                                                                       -- (T-026)
52	    usage_type          TEXT CHECK (usage_type IS NULL OR usage_type IN
53	                            ('code_term','colloquial','regional_variant','outdated_or_disfavoured','product_name')),
54	    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
55	    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
56	    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
57	    updated_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
58	    -- (T-026) an attested occurrence says where; a seed says nowhere.
59	    CHECK (attestation NOT IN ('instrument','other_source')
60	           OR observation_id IS NOT NULL
61	           OR (source_url IS NOT NULL AND (source_page IS NOT NULL OR source_clause IS NOT NULL))),
62	    CHECK (attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')
63	           OR (source_url IS NULL AND source_page IS NULL AND source_line IS NULL AND source_clause IS NULL))
64	);
65	-- One row per OCCURRENCE: the same form in two sources or jurisdictions is two rows.
66	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_term_aliases_occurrence ON term_aliases
67	    (term_id, alias, language, COALESCE(jurisdiction, ''), COALESCE(observation_id, 0),
68	     COALESCE(source_url, ''), COALESCE(source_clause, ''), COALESCE(source_page, ''),
69	     COALESCE(source_line, 0));
70	CREATE INDEX idx_ta_alias    ON term_aliases(alias);      -- recreated (exists today)
71	CREATE INDEX idx_ta_language ON term_aliases(language);   -- recreated (exists today)
72	
73	-- T-026's junction, remapped by key to form_id (section 10, step 3).
74	CREATE TABLE search_execution_forms (
75	    exec_id            INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES search_executions(exec_id),
76	    form_id            INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES term_aliases(form_id),
77	    created_at         TEXT NOT NULL,
78	    created_by_session TEXT NOT NULL,
79	    PRIMARY KEY (exec_id, form_id)
80	);
81	
82	-- The one home of the judge and reason of a label set by judgment (OD-38), and of the label it replaced.
83	CREATE TABLE term_label_picks (
84	    pick_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
85	    term_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
86	    former_label        TEXT,                                 -- the label replaced; NULL only for a mint by add-term --first-form
87	    form_id             INTEGER REFERENCES term_aliases(form_id),          -- rename-term --from-form, or a mint's first form
88	    observation_id      INTEGER REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id), -- rename-term --from-observation
89	    ruling_quote        TEXT,                                               -- rename-term --ruling-quote (found once in the ledger)
90	    judge               TEXT NOT NULL,                        -- who picked
91	    reason              TEXT NOT NULL,                        -- why (add-term --first-form: its --rationale)
92	    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
93	    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,                        -- with whatever else dbcore.stamp_for fills
94	    CHECK ((form_id IS NOT NULL) + (observation_id IS NOT NULL) + (ruling_quote IS NOT NULL) = 1),
95	    CHECK (former_label IS NOT NULL OR form_id IS NOT NULL)
96	);
97	```
98	
99	`term_label_picks` stores no route (derived from which pointer is set, rule 8) and no new label (it is `terms.canonical_en`; the pick reaches it by `term_id`, rule 5). The label a term carried between two picks is the `former_label` of the later one, or `canonical_en` after the last. A mint by `add-term --from-observation` writes no row: its warrant is its `term_adjudications` row. A catalogue mint writes none: its warrant is the catalogue columns on `terms`. Columns on `terms` for the judge and reason were rejected (section 15, G).
100	
101	`usage_type` is nullable: NULL means "not yet typed", which is the truth for every existing row; it is typed by judgment when a row is next touched (T-107), never guessed by the migration. The five values are the sixth statement's list, in the column's own CHECK (read by `dbcore.check_values`, never retyped).
102	
103	## 4. What T-026 builds on this table (as folded 2026-11-13; T-026's section 4 governs its own details)
104	
105	- `attestation TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unrecorded'` with the five-value CHECK above (the sixth statement's four kinds plus `unrecorded`): `instrument` (a code, standard or statute uses the form), `other_source` (any other source uses it: signage manual, public-body or advocacy guidance, a study, a glossary), `owner_supplied` (a seed the owner gave), `model_seed` (a model generated it), `unrecorded` (no provenance). `instrument` and `other_source` are attestations; the other three are seeds or unknowns and are **search aids only** (E4). The `DEFAULT` is required by `ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL`, and T-028's rebuild keeps it (section 10, step 2).
106	- `source_url`, `source_page`, `source_line`, `source_clause`, and the two cross-column CHECKs of section 3, in DDL.
107	- **Mechanical fill**, from what the row already says, in `classify()`'s precedence (`scripts/audit/alias_provenance_audit.py`), by `INSTR`: `VERIFIED-GLOSSARY`, `VERIFIED-CROSS` and `VERIFIED-NATIVE` → `unrecorded` (they carry no observation and no locator, so the first CHECK would refuse `other_source`; the condition this page set on 2026-11-12 came true, and T-026 lists those rows for T-107 to re-attest with a locator); `observation_id` set → `other_source`; `model-generated` → `model_seed`; anything else → `unrecorded`. Never `instrument` by inference.
108	- `add-alias` gains the base route of the seventh statement (`--alias --language --jurisdiction --source-url (--source-page | --source-clause) [--source-line] --attestation instrument|other_source`, the pair checked against `lang_jur_map`) and a seed route (`--seed owner_supplied|model_seed`). The base route's warrant is its locator and its judge is `created_by_session`: no rationale column. The observation route writes `other_source` unless `--attestation instrument` is given.
109	- `alias_provenance_audit` reads `attestation` first and falls back to the notes markers for `unrecorded` rows only, so the curated, repo-shorthand and `VERIFIED-*` classes survive until T-107 re-attests them. T-028 changes nothing in it: it already counts per row, which is per `form_id`.
110	- **The search-forms junction, `search_execution_forms`**, points at a form by `term_aliases`' present key `(term_id, alias, language)` with a real foreign key, not by `rowid`: SQLite cannot declare a foreign key on a rowid (measured: `foreign key mismatch`), and `scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py` diffs a table by its declared key and emits rows without their implicit rowids (`grep -n 'implicit rowids' scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py`), so a rowid captured on a scratch copy can name another row in the canonical database. `log-search --form-id N` takes a rowid as input only and stores the key. T-028 remaps the junction by that key to `form_id` (section 10, step 3).
111	
112	**Why the occurrence grain is T-028's and not T-026's:** T-026 adds columns by `ALTER TABLE` and needs no rebuild; the grain needs one. Until T-028 merges, a second occurrence of a form a term already holds in that language cannot be stored, so **T-107 (attest forms) now waits for T-028** (its task file is corrected in the same pass).
113	
114	## 5. Membership, the legacy `alias_type` values, and conflation
115	
116	- **Members of the equivalence class** are the rows whose `alias_type` is not `NARROWER` or `BROADER`. A `NARROWER` or `BROADER` row is a related search string, not a name of the concept: it is never shown as a name, never counted as a form, never matched as a name. (Term-to-term relations are T-029's table; these strings name no term.)
117	- **`TRANSLATION`, `DEPRECATED`, `DOMAIN` are legacy values.** Each joins a relation with another fact (a seed's origin; a usage; a domain variant). After T-026 and T-028 those facts have typed homes (`attestation`, `usage_type`). The existing rows are **not rewritten** (`DOMAIN` cannot be mapped to a usage without judgment: `select alias, language, notes from term_aliases where alias_type='DOMAIN'`); no writer writes these three values again; no reader infers attestation or usage from them. `add-alias` already refuses `TRANSLATION` and `DEPRECATED`; it now refuses `DOMAIN` too, naming `--usage-type`. `rename-term` stops writing `DEPRECATED` (section 8).
118	- **Conflation is derived, not stored:** a form held as a member by two concepts in one language is a conflation. Query: `select upper(language), alias, group_concat(distinct term_id) from term_aliases where alias_type not in ('NARROWER','BROADER') group by 1, 2 having count(distinct term_id) > 1`. `add-alias` reports it; `add-term` refuses it unless the operator names the other concept with `--distinct-from`; `rename-term` and `mint-term-from-catalogue` refuse a label another concept holds as an attested form, as they do today (section 8; corrected 2026-11-13).
119	
120	## 6. `canonical_en`
121	
122	- **Kept, `NOT NULL`, meaning "our English descriptive label".** Six committed data migrations INSERT `terms.canonical_en` (`git grep -l canonical_en -- 'scripts/migrations/data_*' | wc -l`) and six views read it as a parameter's name (`select name from sqlite_master where type='view' and sql like '%canonical_en%'`); every one keeps working because the column keeps its meaning: a label to show and to search our own registry by. Relaxing `NOT NULL` would rebuild `terms` for no gain once English labels are allowed (eighth statement).
123	- **Never a form.** No writer copies `canonical_en` into `term_aliases`. `rename-term` stops doing so (it wrote the old label as `DEPRECATED`); the former label is recorded once, in `term_label_picks.former_label` (section 3). **Corrected 2026-11-13:** this page first kept it in the `AMENDED` trailer `rename-term` writes on `scope_note`, which the 2026-11-06 schema-shape statement forbids (a correction appended to a note); no route of `rename-term` writes that trailer now, and existing trailers are not rewritten.
124	- **Marked as ours by derivation, not a column** (OD-03: "add no label-kind column"): `v_term_names.label_is_attested_form` is 1 exactly when an attested member form (`instrument` or `other_source`) of the same concept has the label's text. (Named `label_is_instrument_term` until 2026-11-13; it was never restricted to instruments.) Otherwise the label is ours.
125	- **The 94 terms** (`select count(*) from terms`) are unchanged; every one derives `label_is_attested_form = 0` today, because no row is attested yet (`select count(*) from term_aliases where observation_id is not null` prints 0, and T-026's fill adds no locator).
126	- The rule that a label must sit inside an observed phrase (the owner's 2026-09-09 rule, kept 2026-10-09) **still binds when the first form is English**; it is lifted only for a concept whose first form is not English, where the eighth statement allows an English descriptive label.
127	
128	## 7. The name shown: `v_term_names` (E1 derived; sketch)
129	
130	```sql
131	-- sketch: one view, the only reader of "what is this concept called"
132	CREATE VIEW v_term_names AS
133	WITH attested AS (                  -- member forms a source uses; seeds are never vocabulary (E4)
134	    SELECT form_id, term_id, alias, upper(language) AS language, jurisdiction, attestation
135	      FROM term_aliases
136	     WHERE alias_type NOT IN ('NARROWER','BROADER')
137	       AND attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')),
138	en_instrument AS (                  -- English forms an instrument of an owed English-language jurisdiction uses
139	    SELECT a.* FROM attested a
140	     WHERE a.attestation = 'instrument' AND a.language = 'EN'
141	       AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_research_scope r
142	                    WHERE upper(r.language) = 'EN' AND r.jurisdiction = a.jurisdiction)),
143	pick AS (
144	    SELECT t.term_id, t.canonical_en,
145	           (SELECT form_id FROM en_instrument e WHERE e.term_id = t.term_id
146	              AND lower(e.alias) = lower(t.canonical_en) ORDER BY form_id LIMIT 1) AS en_label_form,
147	           (SELECT MIN(form_id) FROM en_instrument e WHERE e.term_id = t.term_id) AS en_first_form,
148	           (SELECT MIN(form_id) FROM attested o WHERE o.term_id = t.term_id
149	              AND o.attestation = 'instrument') AS origin_form
150	      FROM terms t)
151	SELECT p.term_id,
152	       p.canonical_en AS label,
153	       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attested a WHERE a.term_id = p.term_id
154	                 AND lower(a.alias) = lower(p.canonical_en)) AS label_is_attested_form,
155	       CASE WHEN p.en_label_form IS NOT NULL THEN 'english_instrument_label'
156	            WHEN p.en_first_form IS NOT NULL THEN 'english_instrument_form'
157	            WHEN p.origin_form   IS NOT NULL THEN 'origin_instrument_form'
158	            ELSE 'label_ours' END AS display_basis,
159	       COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form) AS display_form_id,
160	       COALESCE((SELECT alias FROM term_aliases f

162	                p.canonical_en) AS display_name,

165	                'EN') AS display_language,
166	       p.origin_form AS origin_form_id

===== term_aliases
CREATE TABLE "term_aliases" (
    form_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    term_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    alias               TEXT NOT NULL,
    language            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EN',
    alias_type          TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK(alias_type IN (
                            'SYNONYM','TRANSLATION','NARROWER',
                            'BROADER','DEPRECATED','DOMAIN'
                        )),
    jurisdiction        TEXT,
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    observation_id      INTEGER REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
    attestation         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unrecorded'
    CHECK (attestation IN ('instrument','other_source','owner_supplied','model_seed','unrecorded')),
    source_url          TEXT
    CHECK (source_url IS NULL OR (
        (source_url GLOB 'http://[^/' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*'
         OR source_url GLOB 'https://[^/' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*')
        AND source_url NOT GLOB '*[' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*')),
    source_page         TEXT
    CHECK (source_page IS NULL OR TRIM(source_page, char(32,9,10,13)) <> ''),
    source_line         INTEGER
    CHECK (source_line IS NULL OR (typeof(source_line) = 'integer' AND source_line > 0)),
    source_clause       TEXT
    CHECK (
        (source_clause IS NULL OR TRIM(source_clause, char(32,9,10,13)) <> '') AND
        -- an attested occurrence says where
        (attestation NOT IN ('instrument','other_source')
         OR observation_id IS NOT NULL
         OR (source_url IS NOT NULL AND (source_page IS NOT NULL OR source_clause IS NOT NULL)))
        -- a seed or an unrecorded form says nowhere
        AND (attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')
         OR (source_url IS NULL AND source_page IS NULL AND source_line IS NULL
             AND source_clause IS NULL))
    ),
    -- the sixth statement of 2026-11-06's usage types, in this column's own CHECK (read by dbcore.check_values)
    usage_type          TEXT
    CHECK (usage_type IS NULL OR usage_type IN
        ('code_term','colloquial','regional_variant','outdated_or_disfavoured','product_name'))
)
===== term_label_picks
CREATE TABLE "term_label_picks" (
    pick_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    term_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    former_label        TEXT,                                               -- NULL only for a mint by add-term --first-form
    form_id             INTEGER REFERENCES term_aliases(form_id),          -- the form the pick rests on
    ruling_quote        TEXT,                                               -- rename-term --ruling-quote
    ref_id              TEXT,                                               -- provenance only (OD-71): no foreign key
    judge               TEXT NOT NULL,                                      -- who picked
    reason              TEXT NOT NULL,                                      -- why (add-term --first-form: its --rationale)
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    CHECK ((form_id IS NOT NULL) + (ruling_quote IS NOT NULL) = 1),
    CHECK (former_label IS NOT NULL OR form_id IS NOT NULL)
)
===== v_term_names
CREATE VIEW v_term_names AS
WITH attested AS (SELECT * FROM v_attested_term_forms),
en_instrument AS (
    SELECT a.* FROM attested a
     WHERE a.attestation = 'instrument' AND a.language = 'EN'
       AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_research_scope r
                    WHERE upper(r.language) = 'EN' AND r.jurisdiction = a.jurisdiction)),
pick AS (
    SELECT t.term_id, t.canonical_en,
           (SELECT form_id FROM en_instrument e WHERE e.term_id = t.term_id
              AND lower(e.alias) = lower(t.canonical_en) ORDER BY form_id LIMIT 1) AS en_label_form,
           (SELECT MIN(form_id) FROM en_instrument e WHERE e.term_id = t.term_id) AS en_first_form,
           (SELECT MIN(form_id) FROM attested o WHERE o.term_id = t.term_id
              AND o.attestation = 'instrument') AS origin_form
      FROM terms t)
SELECT p.term_id,
       p.canonical_en AS label,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attested a WHERE a.term_id = p.term_id
                 AND lower(a.alias) = lower(p.canonical_en)) AS label_is_attested_form,
       CASE WHEN p.en_label_form IS NOT NULL THEN 'english_instrument_label'
            WHEN p.en_first_form IS NOT NULL THEN 'english_instrument_form'
            WHEN p.origin_form   IS NOT NULL THEN 'origin_instrument_form'
            ELSE 'label_ours' END AS display_basis,
       COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form) AS display_form_id,
       COALESCE((SELECT alias FROM term_aliases f
                  WHERE f.form_id = COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form)),
                p.canonical_en) AS display_name,
       COALESCE((SELECT upper(language) FROM term_aliases f
                  WHERE f.form_id = COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form)),
                'EN') AS display_language,
       p.origin_form AS origin_form_id
  FROM pick p
===== v_attested_term_forms
CREATE VIEW v_attested_term_forms AS
-- The forms of a term that name the concept itself and are attested (an instrument or another source): the set
-- v_term_names displays from and scan_debt.py matches a clause against. One home (migration 154).
SELECT form_id, term_id, alias, upper(language) AS language, jurisdiction, attestation
  FROM term_aliases
 WHERE alias_type NOT IN ('NARROWER','BROADER')
   AND attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')
===== base_jurisdictions
CREATE TABLE base_jurisdictions (
    -- THE SHAPE OF A CODE, held by the table where a table can hold it: upper-case letters,
    -- digits and at most one dash, with a letter first; the GB prefix is the ruled rejected
    -- spelling (UK is the project's code). The dash belongs to a sub-national code and to
    -- no other kind, and a sub-national code is exactly <parent_code>-<a non-empty
    -- subdivision>. That the parent is a `country` cannot be a CHECK (it reads another
    -- row); the writer, db.py add-jurisdiction, refuses it.
    jurisdiction_code  TEXT PRIMARY KEY
                       CHECK (jurisdiction_code = UPPER(jurisdiction_code)
                              AND jurisdiction_code NOT LIKE 'GB%'
                              AND jurisdiction_code GLOB '[A-Z]*'
                              AND jurisdiction_code NOT GLOB '*[^A-Z0-9-]*'
                              AND jurisdiction_code NOT GLOB '*-*-*'
                              AND jurisdiction_code NOT GLOB '*-'),
    kind               TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('country', 'sub-national', 'meta')),
    parent_code        TEXT REFERENCES base_jurisdictions(jurisdiction_code),
    admission_ref      TEXT,
    created_at         TEXT,
    created_by_session TEXT,
    CHECK ((kind = 'sub-national') = (parent_code IS NOT NULL)),
    CHECK ((kind = 'sub-national') = (jurisdiction_code LIKE '%-%')),
    CHECK (kind <> 'sub-national'
           OR (substr(jurisdiction_code, 1, length(parent_code) + 1) = parent_code || '-'
               AND length(jurisdiction_code) > length(parent_code) + 1))
)
===== v_research_scope
CREATE VIEW v_research_scope AS
-- v_research_scope: the (language, jurisdiction) pairs the research scope OWES a search for.
--
-- The ONE home of "what is owed": every lang_jur_map row not recorded `scoped-out`. A NULL scope_status is owed --

-- Readers: v_coverage_priority, `db.py coverage`.
SELECT language, jurisdiction, role
  FROM lang_jur_map
 WHERE COALESCE(scope_status, 'in-scope') <> 'scoped-out'

        a combining mark only after a base letter of those three scripts. Everywhere else it is
        the difference between two words: Hindi कि and की, Thai ไม่ and ไม้, Arabic كَتَبَ and
        كُتُبٌ, Japanese か and が verified as one quote when every mark was stripped. The test is

      * ACCENTS FOLD rather than vanish. `Pérez` now normalises to `perez`, not `prez`:

    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", _TAG.sub(" ", text or "")).lower())
    out, marks, word = [], [], False

            # sign, a Thai tone, Arabic or Hebrew pointing, the voicing mark that makes か が). On any
            # other base it is an accent or a stray: `Pérez` meets `Perez`, and the space + accent that

            if word:

    """(readings, pieces) of one number as written. `readings`: a list of frozensets of Decimal,

    three digits after one mark (`1.200`, `1,200`) is AMBIGUOUS and carries both readings. A run that

def _owner_approval(approval_ref: str, subject: str) -> str:
    """The approval heading for a base-vocabulary admission: one dated ledger entry whose heading begins "Owner"
    (the owner's own words). A delegated resolution is a model's, and any other entry (a session, a referral, a
    correction, a supersession record) is not an approval, so each admits nothing."""
    heading = dbcore.require_approval_heading(approval_ref, subject)
    if heading.startswith(dbcore.LEDGER_DELEGATED_PREFIX):
        raise Refusal(f"{subject}: --approval-ref {heading!r} is a delegated resolution (a model's, under the "
                      f"owner's delegation), not the owner's words. This is a decision on research scope or "
                      f"the population taxonomy, and the owner's. Nothing was written.")
    if not heading.startswith(dbcore.LEDGER_OWNER_PREFIX):
        raise Refusal(f"{subject}: --approval-ref {heading!r} is not an entry that records the owner's own words "
                      f"(the ledger's owner entries begin {dbcore.LEDGER_OWNER_PREFIX!r}: Owner answers, Owner "
                      f"statements, Owner rulings). A session heading, a referral to the owner, a correction or "
                      f"a supersession record approves nothing. List them with grep -n '^## Owner' "
                      f"references/project-standards.md. Nothing was written.")
    return heading

#: UNITS AND THEIR EXACT FACTORS ARE ROWS (T-030, migration 149): `base_units` names each unit as a source writes it, the
#: quantity kind it measures (`base_quantity_kinds`, T-020) and its factor to the kind's CANONICAL unit (the unit whose
#: factor is 1) as two integers, so every conversion is exact in Fraction and never a float. A unit is added by a row, not by
#: an edit here. This replaces `NOTATION_FAMILIES` (owner ruling 2026-09-17, "Present both -- don't choose between ratio or
#: percentage", extended to exact length units by OR-10, 2026-10-29): the gradient notations are two rows of the kind
#: `gradient`, and the lengths are rows of the kind `length`.
#:
#: A KIND IS NOT A GUESS ABOUT TWO NOTATIONS. Two units of one kind denote one quantity exactly (a metre is 1000 millimetres;
#: `1:12` is 100/12 percent); units of different kinds never convert (millimetres and percent, or a unit with no row, stay
#: apart and the engine refuses to compose them). `degrees` has no row: it is the ARCTANGENT of the gradient, not a
#: rescaling, so no exact factor relates it to percent.
#:
#: THE ROUNDING RULE, declared once, here (the owner's rulings, OD-22 and OD-42 in references/project-standards.md, "Delegated
#: resolution 2026-11-12 -- OD-22" and "Delegated resolution 2026-11-13 -- OD-42"; both resolved under delegation, the
#: owner's increment being OR-10): a figure shown in a unit of the SAME system as the unit the source stated (a change of
#: metric prefix) keeps the source's digits and is exact. A figure shown in a unit of the OTHER system (inch-foot to metric)
#: is shown at the nearest increment of the shown unit's system that does not fall on the wrong side of the source's
#: bound: a minimum is never shown below it, a maximum never above it; the stored bound stays exact. The increment is the
#: owner's, in the kind's canonical unit (5 mm; a quarter inch is 127/20 mm), keyed by (kind, system). A JUDGED RULE, not a
#: derived one, so it is a typed constant (the NON_QUANTITY_DOMAINS precedent below); a test holds its keys inside the
#: live rows (a renamed kind or system cannot silently disarm it).
SHOWN_STEPS = {("length", "metric"): Fraction(5), ("length", "inch-foot"): Fraction(127, 20)}
_RATIO_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*:\s*(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*$")

UnitRow = namedtuple("UnitRow", "unit kind factor figure_form system")


def load_units(conn):
    """`base_units` as {unit: UnitRow}, ordered by factor then name (the canonical unit first, then up). A kind's
    members are the rows sharing its `kind` -- there is no second list. Raises sqlite3.OperationalError when the table
    is missing: a database without it cannot read a unit, and saying nothing would read every unit as standing alone."""
    return {r[0]: UnitRow(r[0], r[1], Fraction(r[2], r[3]), r[4], r[5]) for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT unit, kind_id, factor_numerator, factor_denominator, figure_form, system FROM base_units "
        "ORDER BY CAST(factor_numerator AS REAL) / factor_denominator, unit")}


def unit_kind(conn, unit):
    """The quantity kind a stated unit measures, or None if it has no row and so stands alone."""
    row = load_units(conn).get((unit or "").strip())
    return row.kind if row else None


def kind_members(conn, kind):
    """The units of a kind, canonical first."""
    return [u for u, r in load_units(conn).items() if r.kind == kind]


def canonical_unit(conn, kind):
    """The unit whose factor is 1 (the unique index allows one). A kind with none cannot be composed, and falling
    through would read a number as if it were already on a scale: refused."""
    for u, r in load_units(conn).items():
        if r.kind == kind and r.factor == 1:
            return u
    raise NotImplementedError(
        "the quantity kind %r has units in base_units but none with factor 1, so no scale to compose on. A unit is a "
        "claim that two notations denote ONE quantity exactly; add the kind's canonical unit (factor 1) by migration, "
        "or remove the kind's units. Falling through would read the number as if it were already canonical." % (kind,))


def _ratio_member(conn, kind):
    """The first unit of `kind` whose figures are written a:b, or None."""
    return next((r for r in load_units(conn).values() if r.kind == kind and r.figure_form == "ratio"), None)


def to_canonical(conn, raw, unit):
    """One stated value -> an exact Fraction on its kind's canonical scale (the factor-1 unit, percent for gradient).

    Exact because it is done in Fraction, never float: `1:12` is 100/12, 8.333... and never rounded here. Rounding
    happens once, at render (`from_canonical`), and is marked inexact when it happens. A unit with no row stands
    alone: the number is read as written, on the scale of the unit itself.
    """
    txt = (raw or "").strip()
    if not txt:
        return None
    row = load_units(conn).get((unit or "").strip())
    if row is not None:

        m = _RATIO_RE.match(txt)

            if run == 0:

            return rise / run * ratio.factor                 # a:b -> the canonical scale, exactly
    try:

    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    return n * row.factor if row is not None and row.figure_form == "number" else n


def _terminating(v):
    """A Fraction as its exact decimal text when it terminates, else None."""
    d = v.denominator
    for p in (2, 5):
        while d % p == 0:
            d //= p
    if d != 1:
        return None
    with localcontext() as ctx:
        ctx.prec = 200
        return format(Decimal(v.numerator) / Decimal(v.denominator), "f")


#: Significant digits a figure that does not terminate in decimal is shown to (8.33333 for 100/12): held once. The digits
#: are cut from the exact Fraction, on the safe side of the bound; no float is ever formatted.
SHOWN_DIGITS = 6


def _decimal_text(v, bound=None):
    """(text, exact) for a Fraction in a unit's own terms, produced from the exact Fraction and never from a float.
    The exact digits when it terminates. When it does not, `SHOWN_DIGITS` significant digits: a `min` is cut upward
    and a `max` downward (never on the wrong side of `v`), no bound to the nearest."""
    t = _terminating(v)
    if t is not None:
        return t, True
    e = 0                                                    # 10**e <= |v| < 10**(e+1), found with integers
    while abs(v) >= 10 ** (e + 1):

    while abs(v) < 10 ** e:

    k = v * scale
    n = math.ceil(k) if bound == "min" else math.floor(k) if bound == "max" else math.floor(k + Fraction(1, 2))
    return _terminating(Fraction(n) / scale), False

#: "the shown figure is marked as converted"). A bound a source wrote in this very unit is `stated`; the rest are derived.
MARK_STATED = "stated"
MARK_CONVERTED = "converted"
MARK_NEAREST = "rounded to the nearest increment"
MARK_UP = "rounded up to the increment"
MARK_DOWN = "rounded down to the increment"
MARK_UNROUNDED = "converted, not rounded (the increment would show zero or cross the other bound)"

    figure would. `mark` is how it was derived (the MARK_ constants). `bound` ('min', 'max' or None for a figure that
    is no bound) and `from_units` (the units in which a source stated this figure) apply `SHOWN_STEPS`: a unit of the
    system a source stated it in is exact; a unit of the other system is shown at the owner's increment on the safe

58	
59	Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.

61	1. **The clause inventory (the owner's route).** One table of clause rows: each row is one clause of one source, keyed by the source (`ref_id`), the locator columns `source_value_extractions` already uses (`locator_scheme`, `loc_*`), the `scan_id` of the reading that recorded it, and the clause's text as held for matching. One home: a figure's extraction points at its clause row, never repeats its locator in a second place it does not already hold. The open pass of a full reading (`source_scans.open_pass_done`) writes the inventory.
62	2. **Held clause text is not shown** (the owner: "clause NOT shown"). No view a page reads selects the clause text; the render task (T-037) reads clause rows only for their locators. A test asserts that no `v_*` view the renderer reads names the text column (derive the renderer's views from T-037 when it lands; until then, from the views whose names the render contract lists).
63	3. **Backed by retained text.** A later parameter is matched first against the inventory, then by a sweep over the retained text (the committed artefact named by the scan's `file_sha256`), and only where neither reaches is the source read again.
64	4. **The re-read flag, derived and not stored** (the owner: "We can flag a source to be read again for later parameters"; smallest change, one home). A pair (source × parameter) is *owed* already, derived by `v_scan_ledger` and printed by `scripts/audit/scan_debt.py` (`DEBT:`). The flag is that derivation narrowed: owed, **and** no inventory row of the source matches the parameter, **and** no retained text is on disk for the source's latest full scan. It is a view (or a `--reread` mode of `scan_debt.py`), never a column or a table of its own, so it cannot drift from the scans; it is cleared by recording the reading (`record-scan --mode targeted`, or `catalogue`). Where a person or model judges that the inventory missed a clause the derivation cannot see, that judgment is an open typed gap on the pair (T-013), not a second flag. Readers: `scan_debt.py`, `v_scan_ledger`, the cell-status verb (T-034), `/run-pipeline`.
65	5. **Duplicate-read minimisation** (the owner: "minimize duplicate reads for efficiency and managing effort"), as one rule in the scan skill and in `record-scan`'s help: before reading a source, list every pair owed for it; read once for all of them (`catalogue` mode) rather than once per parameter; use `targeted` only when exactly one parameter is owed; never re-read a pair already covered by a `full` scan of the same `file_sha256`; a re-read is allowed when the earlier scan was not `full`, the file changed, or the flag of item 4 holds.

- Do not write `data/guidebook.db` except through `migrate_db.py`. Do not run `run_checks.py --all`, `bootstrap.sh` or `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Do not push to `main`, rebase or force-push; do not subscribe to pull-request activity.
- Do not type an id or a count into a test; derive it.

## 9. Stop conditions

Stop and report when: the evidence output differs from section 3; a reader cannot be made to filter without changing what a live check asserts; the owner has answered OI-55 (7) in a form that contradicts item 2's refusal (apply the answer only if it is in the ledger in the owner's words); a check green before is red after; the rebuild does not reproduce the database.

## 10. Rollback

Before merge: close the pull request, delete the branch. After merge: a compensating migration in a new pull request; committed migrations are never edited.

## 11. Adversarial pass and pull request

Real execution only. `/adversarial` once (ask the critic to attack the reader table first); `/batch-done`; push; open the pull request last, once, against the integration base; call `unsubscribe_pr_activity` for it immediately; push nothing afterwards except a deliberate change, never `[skip ci]` on the final push. One pull request merges at a time; re-derive the migration number after `git merge "$BASE"` if another merged first.
----
1. Run `/adversarial` once on the finished diff (a read-only critic attacks the claim, then you repair). One pass; no pass on the pass. For a research task the pass is recorded in the database with `db.py record-adversarial-pass` and closed with `close-adversarial-pass`.
2. Run `/batch-done`; it is the only definition of finished.
3. Push the branch. Open the pull request **last**, once, against the integration base (section 2). Title = the commit subject. Body: the problem; the evidence before and after; each caller the sweep found and what was done to it; each check you ran with its `EXAMINED:` line, before and after; the c
4. Immediately after creating the pull request call `unsubscribe_pr_activity` for it (creating a pull request subscribes the session by itself). Do not watch it, do not poll, do not schedule a reminder. Push nothing afterwards except a deliberate change; the final push is never `[skip ci]`.
5. One pull request merges at a time. If another task's pull request merged while you worked, take it with `git merge "$BASE"` after `git fetch origin` (never rebase) and, if you carry a schema migration, derive its number again by the rule in section 4.

## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.

1. **One shared refusal, two callers.** Move the refusals `insert_parameter` runs on the kind and its warrant (T-020 section 4 item 1a: no kind or an unknown kind, naming every kind read from `base_quantity_kinds`; no observation id; an unknown observation id; an observation whose `context_quote` states no value) into one function in `scripts/db.py` (for example `_kind_refusal(conn, kind, observation_id)`), called by `insert_parameter` unchanged in order and message. Reuse; do not write a second copy (T-041's rule, one home for helpers).
2. **`db.py set-parameter-kind --parameter-id N --quantity-kind K --quantity-kind-observation-id O --session S [--dry-run]`** (function `set_parameter_kind`). It runs, in this order: the parameter exists and is `active` (`_parameter_row`; a retired or merged parameter is refused, naming its survivor for a merge); the shared refusal of item 1; **the kind is not already set** (write-once; the refusal names the stored kind and its observation); **no live determination and no open gate stands on the parameter** (`_refuse_live_work`, `grep -n 'def _refuse_live_work' scripts/db.py`). Then one `UPDATE` of the two columns with the `updated_*` stamp (`_updated(conn, "base_parameters", session, stamp)`, the helper `retire-parameter` uses).
   **Chosen (authoring 2026-11-13):** write-once. Rejected: an overwrite with a reason (a kind that changes under a parameter changes what every stored figure of it means; a wrong kind is a new decision recorded as such, and no such case exists yet, so the path is not built: CLAUDE.md §8, nothing is added without naming what reads it). **Chosen:** refuse while a live determination or open gate stands, as `retire-parameter` does: a determination computed before its parameter had a kind would silently gain one. No live determination exists today (`select count(*) from specifications where retired_at is null`), so the refusal changes no present act. **Chosen:** the flag spelling `--quantity-kind-observation-id`, so T-109's own precondition command finds the verb. **Chosen:** a new verb rather than a flag on `annotate-parameter` (that verb appends a dated line to `notes` and nothing else, `grep -n 'def annotate_parameter' -A8 scripts/db.py`; giving it a typed write would make one verb do two kinds of act, and its "any status" rule is wrong for a kind).
3. **No row is written by this task.** T-109 writes the kinds (research, rule 10).

**What reads what this task adds:** T-109 (its precondition, then its rows); `workplan/pipeline-state-graph/machines.yaml` if it lists the parameter verbs (the sweep says). **What it makes deletable:** nothing; it removes the only reason T-109 would reach for hand SQL.

**Code size.** Report `git diff --shortstat "$(git merge-base HEAD "$BASE")" -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'` after `git add`.


Real execution only. `/adversarial` once; `/batch-done`; push; open the pull request last, once, against the integration base; call `unsubscribe_pr_activity` for it immediately; push nothing afterwards except a deliberate change, never `[skip ci]` on the final push.

**Amended 2026-11-19 (T-083 and its repair, migrations 155 and 156; owner statements 2026-11-18, OD-71):** `base_parameters.quantity_kind_observation_id` and the flag `--quantity-kind-observation-id` no longer exist: a base table holds no pointer into the evidence stage. ## 1. The five operations

The single most useful distinction: **discovery produces _sources_, extraction produces _values_,
synthesis produces _statements_.** Confusing them is what lets a source be "processed" in one sense
and untouched in another.

| # | Operation | Consumes | Produces | Output table | Log of the act |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Search execution** | a query × index × language × jurisdiction | screened results | `search_candidates` | `search_executions` |

def _non_member_types(conn):
    """The alias_type values that are related search strings, not names of the concept (design section 5),
    read from their one home: the `alias_type NOT IN (...)` of v_attested_term_forms, the set v_term_names reads

    sql = conn.execute("SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='view' AND name='v_attested_term_forms'").fetchone()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""scripts/dbcore.py — the one place this repository opens, stamps and keys the database.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Measured 2026-08-25: 104 raw `sqlite3.connect(` call sites across 55 live
files, 48 independent resolutions of GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH, and 37+ files computing their own
repo root -- while `scripts/db.py` already held a correct connect() that NOTHING IMPORTED.
Every lesson that connect() had learned (read-only URI, query_only, the journal_mode trap
below) was therefore un-inherited by 55 files. Owner directive 2026-08-25: "we only need one
set of tools that manages how to write to a table, read a table, and cross-reference them."

WHAT BELONGS HERE: mechanics. Connection, paths, audit stamps, the case-folded join keys, the
reference-id rules, and the one list of tables a session may write.

WHAT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT, each for a reason that outlives this docstring:
  * schemas/*.py Pydantic mirrors -- "schema drift is a bug, not a convention" (CLAUDE.md §8)
    only works while the mirror is independent of the thing it mirrors.
  * scripts/research/retrieval_log.py -- its whole value is being OUTSIDE the write path.
    `--verify-authors` diffs stored rows against the bytes actually received; a writer that
    verifies itself verifies nothing.
  * Check and audit SQL -- a gate that imports the library it polices fails together with it.
    Rule 5 forbids two STORED homes of a fact, not two independent COMPUTATIONS of it;
    re-derivation is precisely what a gate is for.
  * emit_data_migration.py / migrate_db.py internals -- the sanctioned write pair works.
  * Query/business logic -- that stays in db.py. This module is mechanics, not model.

IMPORTING IT. Consumers need one preamble, because you cannot import a shared module without
first locating it:

    import sys; from pathlib import Path
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N] / "scripts"))
    import dbcore

That relative hop is the one piece of boilerplate consolidation cannot remove. It replaces
3-6 lines of per-file path/root/connect duplication and is identical everywhere but `N`.
"""

## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

A concept's displayed name is the name a page prints for it. Today `v_term_names` picks it by form number (`MIN(form_id)`), so a lower-numbered form recorded later, or any second English code, renames the concept with no judge; the ledger forbids exactly that ("Do not choose the displayed name by `MIN(form_id)` or by recency", ACTION (2) of "Owner statements 2026-11-18 — OD-71 …"). The owner's rule (OD-72, ratified 2026-11-19) counts the attested appearances of each way of writing the name, puts a CSA or ISO form first, shows our label and owes a judge on a tie, and lets a named judge's pick override. Two facts it needs are not held: which body issued the instrument an occurrence was read in (CSA has no row anywhere; a URL substring is not a warrant), and a grouping key no view can compute (SQLite's `lower()` folds ASCII only, and the project's one normaliser, `retrieval_log.normalise_quote`, applies NFKC, which SQL cannot).

**Evidence command** (read-only):
```
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute(\"select count(*) from term_aliases where attestation in ('instrument','other_source')\").fetchone(), c.execute(\"select jurisdiction_code, kind from base_jurisdictions where jurisdiction_code in ('ISO','CSA')\").fetchall(), [r[1] for r in c.execute('pragma table_info(term_aliases)') if 'body' in r[1]], c.execute(\"select lower('ÄSS'), count(*) from sqlite_master where name='v_term_names' and sql like '%MIN(form_id)%'\").fetchone())"
```
**Output on 2026-11-19:** `(0,) [('ISO', 'meta')] [] ('Äss', 1)`: no attested form (the rule has no live subject, as the adjudication says); ISO is a meta jurisdiction and CSA is no row (as the adjudication says); no body column; `lower()` leaves `Ä` unfolded; the view orders by `MIN(form_id)`. It agrees with the adjudication. If any part differs, stop (section 9). If the first figure is above 0, the occurrences already recorded carry no body: stop.

## 4. The change

Order of preference (CLAUDE.md §8): do nothing; change a rule; reuse; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code. Nothing can be "done nothing": the view is a rule the ledger forbids, and the priority needs a fact no cell holds.

1. **One base table, `base_issuing_bodies`: the vocabulary of issuing bodies, held as rows, extended by data with a warrant** (the adjudication: "a foreign key into a bodies vocabulary held as rows"; rule 8: no list in code). Columns: `body_code TEXT PRIMARY KEY` with a CHECK that it is upper case, starts with a letter and holds only letters, digits and dashes; `name_as_written TEXT NOT NULL` (the body's name as its document writes it; non-blank CHECK); the warrant in the row's own cells (OD-71): `source_url TEXT NOT NULL` (`http`/`https`, no whitespace), `source_page TEXT`, `source_clause TEXT`, one of the two non-blank, `source_quote TEXT NOT NULL` (the words of the document naming its issuer; the adjudication's item 12, "the words the base cell asserts were found"); `terminology_priority INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (terminology_priority IN (0,1))`; `priority_approval_ref TEXT`, with `CHECK ((terminology_priority = 1) = (priority_approval_ref IS NOT NULL))`; `created_at`, `created_by_session` NOT NULL. Which bodies take priority is a column on the row, set with the owner's ledger entry; the code never names CSA or ISO. **No `jurisdiction_code` column:** nothing reads one (§8). A body is not a jurisdiction: CSA is not added to `base_jurisdictions` (jurisdiction is the owner's, CLAUDE.md §8).
2. **One column, `term_aliases.issuing_body TEXT REFERENCES base_issuing_bodies(body_code)`**, by `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` (default NULL), with the CHECK `(issuing_body IS NULL OR attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')) AND (attestation <> 'instrument' OR issuing_body IS NOT NULL)`: a seed or an unrecorded form names no body, and an instrument occurrence always does (every code, standard or statute has an issuer; a NULL would drop a CSA form's priority silently). An `other_source` occurrence may name one. If SQLite refuses a CHECK that names `attestation` in `ADD COLUMN` on the scratch copy, the DDL keeps the foreign key only, the two conditions go into the shared writer refusal of item 4, and the pull request says so; do not rebuild `term_aliases` in this task.
3. **The rule, one home: `term_names(conn, term_ids=None)` in `scripts/db.py`** (query logic belongs in `db.py`, `sed -n 22,24p scripts/dbcore.py`; it loads the normaliser through the existing `_retrieval_log()`, never a second normaliser). It returns, per term: `term_id`, `label` (`canonical_en`), `label_is_attested_form`, `display_name`, `display_language`, `display_basis`, `judge_owed` (0 or 1), and `display_form_ids` (the occurrences whose written text is shown; empty when the label is shown). Its input is the attested member forms, read only through `v_attested_term_forms` (one home of "attested" and of the member rule); `model_seed`, `owner_supplied` and `unrecorded` rows never count (E4). In order:
   a. **A named judge's pick overrides.** A term with a `term_label_picks` row whose `former_label IS NOT NULL` (a pick by `rename-term`; a mint by `add-term --first-form` has `former_label` NULL and is not a pick of the name) shows `canonical_en`, the cell the pick wrote, basis `judge_pick`, `judge_owed` 0. No pick row is ordered by number or time: the label cell already holds the pick in force. This is the owner's "preferred display term column" (OD-72 (4)); no display cell is stored.
   b. **The counting set.** If the term has an attested `instrument` form in `EN` of a jurisdiction that `v_research_scope` holds with language `EN`, the set is its attested forms in `EN`; otherwise it is its attested forms in every language (OD-72 (6): "a concept with no attested English instrument form of an in-scope jurisdiction is counted across its attested forms in every language"; the first branch is E1's, `grep -n -E '^\| E1 ' references/project-standards.md`). No date of attestation is read.
   c. **Groups.** A group is (`upper(language)`, `normalise_quote(alias).casefold()`). Its count is the number of occurrence rows in the counting set. *This file's reading, to be held exactly:* the count of a group is all its attested occurrences in the set, and the priority of item d only narrows which groups may win.
   d. **CSA or ISO wins outright.** If any group holds an occurrence whose `issuing_body` row has `terminology_priority = 1`, only such groups compete; among several, the count decides (OD-72 (2)).
   e. **The count decides; a tie owes a judge.** One group with the highest count wins. An exact tie at the top shows `canonical_en`, basis `tie_label`, `judge_owed` 1; never `MIN(form_id)`. *This file's reading:* the text shown for a winning group is the written form (`alias`, verbatim) with the most occurrences inside the group, because a normalised key is a string no source wrote; an exact tie inside the group is a tie (label, `judge_owed` 1).
   f. **No attested form:** `canonical_en`, basis `label_ours`, `judge_owed` 0.

              "--field comparator`), do not widen the interval here"), None

    # ── PRESENT BOTH ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Every notation the governing set states, carrying the SELECTED bound. A notation
    # is `stated` when some governing claim wrote this very bound that way, and
    # `derived` when the engine rendered it -- and a derived rendering that does not
    # terminate is marked inexact, because ACTION (3) forbids a rounded figure standing
    # where a source's own figure would. 1:12 is 8.333...% and this says so.
    notations = None
    if family:
        _lo_from = {u for b, u in bounds if vmin is not None and b[0] == vmin}
        _hi_from = {u for b, u in bounds if vmax is not None and b[1] == vmax}
        # A POINT is ONE claim that states one value (both bounds are its own): shown at the nearest increment on both
        # ends. A floor and a ceiling that merely coincide are two claims: the minimum is still never shown below its
        # source and the maximum never above (OD-22: "a minimum never shows below the source, a maximum never above
        # it"), the rule is dbcore.SHOWN_STEPS.
        _point = vmin is not None and any(b[0] == vmin and b[1] == vmin for b, _u in bounds)
        _lo_kind, _hi_kind = (None, None) if _point else ("min", "max")

        def _num(text):
            try:
                return Fraction(text)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                return None                    # an a:b figure is no number to order

        notations = []
        for member in kind_members(conn, family):
            if member not in stated_notations:
                continue                      # the governing set never used it
            lo = from_canonical(conn, vmin, member, _lo_kind, _lo_from)
            hi = from_canonical(conn, vmax, member, _hi_kind, _hi_from)
            _a, _b = _num(lo[0]), _num(hi[0])
            _crossed = _a is not None and _b is not None and _a > _b

                # the increment cannot hold both bounds on their safe sides (a minimum rounded up passes a maximum
                # rounded down): show the exact conversion of each, which is on no wrong side, and say so
                lo = from_canonical(conn, vmin, member, _lo_kind, ())
                hi = from_canonical(conn, vmax, member, _hi_kind, ())
            lo_mark = None if lo[0] is None else MARK_STATED if member in _lo_from else (MARK_UNROUNDED if _crossed else lo[2])
            hi_mark = None if hi[0] is None else MARK_STATED if member in _hi_from else (MARK_UNROUNDED if _crossed else hi[2])
            notations.append({
                "notation": member,
                "min": lo[0], "max": hi[0],
                # each bound says how it was reached: `stated` (a source wrote this bound in this unit) or derived,
                # with the rounding direction, because no source stated 765 mm for a bound it stated as 30 in
                "min_mark": lo_mark, "max_mark": hi_mark,
                "stated": all(m == MARK_STATED for m in (lo_mark, hi_mark) if m is not None),
                "exact": bool(lo[1] and hi[1]),
            })
        if len(notations) > 1:
            caveat = ((caveat + "; ") if caveat else "") + (
                "value presented in %d notations of one quantity (owner ruling "
                "2026-09-17: present both, never choose)" % len(notations))
        if stated_notations - {unit}:
            caveat = ((caveat + "; ") if caveat else "") + (
                "the headline is in %s, the canonical unit of its kind, converted from the stated %s"
                % (unit, ", ".join(sorted(repr(u) for u in stated_notations))))

    return (float(vmin) if vmin is not None else None,
            float(vmax) if vmax is not None else None,
            unit, caveat, notations)

A concept's displayed name is the name a page prints for it. OD-72 counts the attested appearances of each way of writing the name, puts a form attested in a CSA or ISO instrument first, shows our label and owes a judge on a tie, and lets a named judge's pick override. Two facts it needs are not held: which body issued the instrument an occurrence was read in, warranted by that instrument's own words (CSA has no row anywhere; a URL substring is not a warrant), and the grouping key, which no view can compute (SQLite's `lower()` folds ASCII only, and the project's one normaliser applies NFKC, which SQL has not).

**Evidence command** (read-only):

Order of preference (CLAUDE.md §8): do nothing; change a rule; reuse; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code. The view is a rule the ledger forbids, and the priority needs a fact no cell holds, so "do nothing" fails.

1. **One base table, `base_issuing_bodies`: the vocabulary of issuing bodies, held as rows, extended by data with a warrant** (the adjudication: "a foreign key into a bodies vocabulary held as rows"; rule 8: no list in code). Which bodies take priority is a cell on the row, set with the owner's ledger entry; no code names CSA or ISO. **One home, and ISO's two rows (rule 5).** `base_jurisdictions` holds ISO as a meta jurisdiction: a place research is owed. This table holds ISO as an issuer of documents. They are two facts with two homes; nothing is copied between them and no pointer is added, because nothing reads one (§8). CSA is not added to `base_jurisdictions` (jurisdiction is the owner's, CLAUDE.md §8).

CHECKs: `(issuing_body IS NULL) = (issuing_body_quote IS NULL)`; `issuing_body IS NULL OR attestation = 'instrument'` (only an instrument occurrence names an issuer); `attestation <> 'instrument' OR issuing_body IS NOT NULL` (every instrument occurrence does: every code, standard or statute has an issuer, and a NULL would drop a CSA or ISO form's priority silently); `(retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL)` and `(retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL)`, each non-blank when set. Cells with linear units only produce byte-identical output (`T143-08`).
   **Storage, per bound.** T-137 as it stands (`grep -n -F "in the row's \\`value_unit\\`" workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-137-units-and-kinds-as-data.md`) stores each bound as the text `str(Fraction)` prints, **in the row's `value_unit`**, under a CHECK of that shape; the engine chooses `value_unit` (today the kind's canonical unit: `grep -n -F "the canonical unit of its kind" scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`). Per bound: (i) governed by a percent or ratio figure, or by an angle in {−45°, 0°, 45°}: the exact canonical Fraction, `value_unit` the canonical unit, as T-137; (ii) governed by an angle at any other value: no exact canonical value exists, so **the one reading the coordinator must confirm:** the cell stores its bounds in that tangent unit (`value_unit` its spelling, each bound the exact Fraction of its figure there: `4.8` is `24/5`, which T-137's CHECK already admits, so no CHECK change is owed) when every stored bound is exact in that unit (stated in it, absent, or 0 or 100 % or `1:1`); otherwise (iii) both bounds are NULL, and the engine does what it does with any NULL pair today: the cell is written `provisional` with a note saying why (T-030's evidence shows that shape: `('provisional', None, None, "governing claims are stated in different units …")`), every governing figure and its converted notations shown. The alternative, a unit per bound, is a column this file does not name. If the coordinator does not confirm, stop before item 3.
4. **`add-unit --conversion`** (choices from the CHECK, `dbcore.schema_choices("base_units", "conversion")`, default `linear`), on the verb T-137 adds. Refusals, in words before a constraint would raise: `tangent_degrees` with a factor given (item 1); for a kind with no ratio-form unit (naming that unit first); with `--figure-form ratio` or a `--system`. **The warrant of a tangent unit.** The conversion is the ratified rule of the adjudication's item 32 ("percent = 100·tan(θ)"), a fact of mathematics, so no source is asked to state an equivalence; T-137's factor test ("a quote that does not state the factor") does not apply to it. What the source warrants is its own use of the spelling with a number for a slope: the quote holds a valued figure in the new spelling, read by T-137's shared figure reader (`grep -n -F "The shared figure reader" workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-137-units-and-kinds-as-data.md`), the branch T-137 already gives a kind's first unit, and the adjudication's item 41 ("a number followed by a unit of the declared kind"). *Derived reading, flagged:* items 31 to 36 state no warrant for a non-linear unit, so the coordinator confirms this one with item 3's. **Spellings in any language** (`°`, `度`, `градус`, `grad`) are added to the one tangent unit by T-137's `add-unit-spelling` (judged; its quote holds the spelling; no numeral asked), never as second units: each is data with a warrant, no list in code. A spelling with no row stands alone, as T-137 leaves any unplaced unit (the adjudication's item 34 is the research that places them).
5. **No row is written by this task.** The tangent unit and its spellings land in a research pull request (rule 10); the four live degree figures of section 3 compose once that row exists and parameter 3 carries the gradient kind (T-109).

'''
s=s[:a0]+new+s[a1:]
s=s.replace("the `figure_refusal` branch by `add-extraction`.","the kind condition of item 2a by the engine.")
open(p,'w').write(s)
